verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, the deponent above-named, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs {para_knowledge_basis} of the above affidavit are true to my personal knowledge; the contents of paragraphs {para_information_basis} are true to my information and belief, the source whereof is stated therein; and the contents of paragraphs {para_records_basis} are true from records maintained in the ordinary course. No part of this affidavit is false and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Deponent
prompt_context: Draft a standard Affidavit in Support of [supporting document]. An affidavit is a written statement of fact, sworn or affirmed by the deponent before a person authorised to administer oaths (Notary Public under the Notaries Act 1952, Oath Commissioner, or Magistrate). It must conform to Order XIX of the CPC for civil matters and analogous provisions in criminal practice. KEY STRUCTURE: (1) cause title (Court · Case · Parties); (2) heading 'AFFIDAVIT'; (3) deponent identification block ('I, [name], S/o [parent], aged [x], occupation [y], resident of [z], do hereby state and affirm on oath as under:'); (4) numbered paragraphs, one fact per paragraph; (5) each paragraph should disclose source — 'I am the petitioner herein and am acquainted with the facts of the case' for knowledge paragraphs; 'I have been informed by [source] and verily believe to be true' for information paragraphs; 'I have perused the records' for records paragraphs; (6) verification clause specifying which paragraphs are on knowledge vs information vs records; (7) deponent signature with date and place; (8) attestation block for Notary / Oath Commissioner / Magistrate. CRITICAL: do NOT mix sources — courts strike down affidavits that fail to identify source of belief (Padmabati Dasi v. Rasik Lal Dhar (1910) 37 Cal 259; A.K.K. Nambiar v. UoI (1969) 3 SCC 864).
promptInstructions: Draft an Affidavit in Support of the document specified (e.g. bail application, interim application, writ petition).
Open with cause title — court, case title, case number.
Deponent identification: 'I, {deponent_name}, S/o {parentage}, aged about {age} years, by occupation {occupation}, resident of {address}, do hereby state and affirm on oath as under:'

Open paragraph (Para 1): establish deponent's locus — 'I am the petitioner / applicant / authorised representative of the petitioner herein and am acquainted with the facts of the case and competent to swear this affidavit.'
Convert each fact in {affidavit_paragraphs} into a separate numbered paragraph.
Each paragraph must clearly disclose the source basis (knowledge / information & belief / records).
Add verification clause specifying paragraph ranges per source — use the {para_knowledge_basis}, {para_information_basis}, {para_records_basis} fields.
Cite A.K.K. Nambiar v. UoI (1969) 3 SCC 864 standards — do NOT mix sources within a paragraph.
Include signature block: 'Deponent' with name, date, place.
Include notary / oath commissioner attestation block per {notarisation_required}.
Do NOT add a prayer clause — affidavits do not contain prayers (the supporting document carries the prayer).

sections.description: Affidavits to be confined to facts deponent can prove on personal knowledge
Functions of notaries — administering oaths and affirmations
Oaths and affirmations replacing Indian Oaths Act framework where applicable

filing_checklist: Original affidavit on stamp paper / plain paper as per court rules
Notary stamp + seal + register entry number
Court fee as per court schedule
Photograph of deponent (where required — typically HC writs)
Identity proof of deponent at time of attestation
Sworn before authorised attestor (Notary / Oath Commissioner / Magistrate)

para_knowledge_basis must be non-empty (every affidavit must have at least some knowledge-paragraphs)
if para_information_basis is specified, the affidavit body must disclose the source for each information-paragraph
